'''Edgar Henry Brown, Jr.''' (December 27, 1926 – December 22, 2021)<ref name="brandeis">{{cite web| url=http://people.brandeis.edu/~brown/|title=Edgar H. Brown. Jr.|publisher=[[Brandeis University]]|access-date=January 21, 2021}}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]] specializing in [[algebraic topology]], and for many years a professor at [[Brandeis University]].<ref>{{cite news| title=BROWN, Edgar H. Jr. |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/bostonglobe/name/edgar-brown-obituary?id=31993374 | newspaper=[[Boston Globe]] |access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref>

==Life==
Brown was born in [[Oak Park, Illinois|Oak Park]], [[Illinois]].<ref name="brandeis" /> He completed his bachelor's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Wisconsin]] in 1949. He completed his master's degree in mathematics at [[Washington State University]] in 1951.

==Career==
He completed his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1954. His doctoral supervisor was [[George W. Whitehead]], and his doctoral dissertation was on ''Finite Computability of the Homotopy Groups of Finite Groups''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|1465}}</ref>

In 1962–63, he visited the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/edgar-h-brown| title=Past member: Edgar H. Brown | date=December 9, 2019 |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] | access-date=January 21, 2021}}</ref> and in 1964 he received the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/edgar-h-brown-jr/ | title=Edgar H. Brown, Jr. | publisher=Guggenheim Memorial Foundation | website=[[Archive.org]] | access-date=December 20, 2016 | archive-date=December 20, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220143955/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/edgar-h-brown-jr/ | url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1974<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=3786119|title=List of Members by Classes September 1, 1997|journal=Records of the Academy (American Academy of Arts and Sciences)|year=1996|issue=1996/1997|pages=56–128}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.

He died on December 22, 2021, just before his 95th birthday, as a Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at Brandeis University.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.brandeis.edu/faculty-senate/in-memoriam/pdfs/memoriam-2021-22/memorial-edgar-brown-professor-emeritus-of-mathematics-daniel-ruberman-professor-mathematics.pdf | title=Memorial: Edgar Brown, Professor Emeritus of Mathematics | first=Daniel | last=Ruberman | publisher=[[Brandeis University]] | format=PDF | date=2021 | access-date=October 25, 2025 }}</ref>

==Contributions to mathematics==
He made numerous contributions to mathematics, including:

* [[Brown's representability theorem]]
* [[Brown–Peterson cohomology]]
* [[Brown–Gitler spectrum]]

His publications include:

*{{cite journal|last= Brown|first= Edgar H. Jr.| title= Twisted tensor products. I. |journal= [[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=69 |year=1959|issue=1 |pages= 223–246 |doi=10.2307/1970101 |jstor= 1970101|mr=0105687}}
*{{cite journal|last= Brown|first= Edgar H. Jr.| title= Cohomology theories |journal= [[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=75 |year=1962|issue=3 |pages= 467–484 |doi=10.2307/1970209 |jstor= 1970209|mr=0138104}}
*{{cite journal|last1= Brown|first1= Edgar H. Jr.| last2= Peterson|first2= Franklin P. |author2-link=Franklin P. Peterson| title=A spectrum whose <math>\mathbb{Z}_p</math> cohomology is the algebra of reduced <math>p^{\rm th}</math> powers |journal= [[Topology (journal)|Topology]] |volume= 5 |year= 1966 |pages=149–154
|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(66)90015-2|mr= 0192494|issue= 2|doi-access= free}}

*{{cite journal| last1=Brown | first1=Edgar H. | title=Abstract homotopy theory | year=1965 | journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume=119 | issue=1| pages=79–85 | url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1965-119-01/S0002-9947-1965-0182970-6/ | doi=10.2307/1994231| jstor=1994231 | doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}
